paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum–Classical Support Vector Machines for Financial Regime Detection: Performance and Efficiency Evaluation

summary: The paper studies a 6-qubit QSVC with a ZZFeatureMap and fidelity kernel on a noiseless statevector simulator, achieving 66.0% test accuracy and 85.3% training accuracy on financial regime classification. The best classical baseline is an RBF SVM at 80.43% accuracy, while hybrid ensembles reach 75.9% (50-50) and 75.4% (60-40), improving minority-class F1 but not surpassing the classical model.

experiments.description: Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) for financial regime classification using a 6-qubit ZZFeatureMap and fidelity-based quantum kernel on standardized macro-financial features.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) with Fidelity Statevector Kernel

hyperparameters.training_subset_size: ~3000 samples (reported as approximately 3,000; also 3,500 in results for scaled run)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Six standardized PCA components were mapped to six qubits; ZZFeatureMap used pairwise ZZ phase interactions with full entanglement.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary market-regime classification via maximum-margin SVM in quantum feature space; kernel K(x_i,x_j)=|<phi(x_i)|phi(x_j)>|^2.

problem_instance.description: Financial regime detection for U.S. market states (Bullish vs Bearish) using multi-asset macro-financial indicators.
problem_instance.dataset_name: SPY, VIX, 10Y Treasury yield, 2Y Treasury yield, ICE BofA High-Yield credit spread, DXY

dataset_specification.description: Bloomberg and FRED data merged on daily timestamps; training period 2006-2022, testing period 2023-2025; chronological 80/20 split; binary labels Bearish (-1) and Bullish (+1)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Returns, rolling volatility (20/60-day), z-scores, momentum (20/60-day), trend ratios, volatility-of-volatility, skewness, kurtosis, liquidity stress proxy for SPY; winsorization at 1st/99th percentiles; z-score standardization; PCA to 6 components; SMOTE oversampling ratio 0.6; chronological split
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Held-out test set evaluation; accuracy, precision, recall, F1; confusion matrices; training vs test accuracy; comparison to classical and hybrid models

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical SVM optimization over quantum kernel matrix
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: StandardScaler, PCA to 6 components, SMOTE oversampling, chronological split
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Predictions evaluated with accuracy/precision/recall/F1 and confusion matrices
implementation_details.total_execution_time: ~1 hour training on average for the full QSVC run; ~3 minutes for kernel evaluation in one reported run
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: Kernel evaluation dominates runtime; approximately 12.25 million pairwise state overlaps reported for the 3,500-sample run

results.unit: minutes (kernel evaluation time in one reported run)
ratio (minority-class F1 in earlier smaller run)
% (described as current achievable boundary / quantum performance envelope)

speedup_claims.conditions: implemented QSVC on a noiseless statevector simulator with O(n^2) kernel evaluation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper emphasizes quadratic kernel-matrix cost and reports substantial runtime overhead; no quantum advantage is demonstrated for the implemented QSVC.

speedup_claims.factor: poly(log N, log d) under ideal assumptions
speedup_claims.conditions: requires efficient QRAM, sparse and well-conditioned matrices, and accurate amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.caveats: This is discussed as background theory from prior QSVM literature, not shown in the experiment.

complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: ~12.25 million pairwise state overlaps (reported for scaled run)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: ~3 minutes for kernel evaluation; ~1 hour average end-to-end training in one reported run
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: <1 minute for classical baselines; ~1 second for classical SVM in efficiency comparison

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require fault-tolerant quantum hardware, efficient data loading, and substantially larger problem sizes than the reported 3,000-3,500 sample runs

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical SVM ensemble combining a classical RBF SVM with a QSVC using hard voting and weighted voting variants (50-50, 60-40, 70-30).

algorithm.ansatz: Classical SVM with RBF kernel plus QSVC with ZZFeatureMap

problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary regime classification with ensemble aggregation of classical and quantum predictions.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Deterministic hard voting and manually specified weighted voting (50-50, 60-40, 70-30)
